title: Presence pulse, lease generation and audience projection v1
description: The three records D-073 needs and the repository lacked: what a qualifying native pulse is, how a lease generation bounds it, and what an authorized viewer is shown. docs/product/PRODUCT_SPEC.md and docs/privacy/PRIVACY_CONTRACT.md are the normative owners, packages/schemas/planning-schema.sql#presence_leases and #presence_events are the persistence owners, and the presence-lease machine owns the lifecycle. A pulse carries no content of any kind: it names a device, a generation and a boolean, never what the device was doing. This is not a presence history — ADR-019 accepts a live-sampling risk on the stated basis that none is stored, so pulses are discarded when their generation closes and packages/schemas/data-disposition-v1.json records no-retention.

thresholds.description: The three D-073 numbers, each bound to the policy key that carries it. Two of those keys used to be misnamed: presence_lease_expiry_seconds held 90 and meant the idle threshold, presence_idle_after_seconds held 300 and meant the offline threshold, and D-385 stated the binding rather than renaming them because a list in scripts/repository/validate_planning_artifacts.py required the old spellings. Reading the registry straight therefore gave idle at 300 and expiry at 90, which is a lease that expires before it can ever go idle and an idle state nothing can reach. PF-026 performed the rename D-385 named as its own reopen condition, so the const bindings below and the values now say the same thing.

lease_generation.description: The generation the pulse was minted under. A daemon restart mints a new one, so a pulse naming a superseded generation is discarded rather than applied, which is what stops a resumed process from reviving an expired lease.

qualifying.description: Whether the device was doing work that counts toward presence. It is a boolean and not a description because a description would be content, and content never crosses the device boundary.

source.description: Only a native collector produces a qualifying pulse. A hosted-web session is never one: a browser tab open on a leaderboard is not evidence that the participant is working, and treating it as such would make presence a measure of who is looking at the product.

lease.description:
The current server-derived answer for one device. The state is derived from the pulse stream and the two thresholds; a client never selects it, exactly as public evidence status is never client-selected.

PF-026 removed `visibility` from this record and from packages/schemas/planning-schema.sql#presence_leases. Visibility is an independent policy and not a state — that part was right — but it is one policy per account, and it was stored once per device against a projection that produces one answer for the whole account. Two devices could hold different values with nothing saying which the merge takes, so going private on a laptop while a desktop stayed authorized published the participant anyway. It lives on profiles.presence_visibility, and this record carries only what the device observed.

audience_projection.description: What one viewer is shown about one subject at one moment. It is computed at display and delivery rather than stored, because a stored projection is a cached authorization decision and D-386 makes every such decision recheck current state.

subject_visibility.description: The subject's account-scoped presence policy, read from profiles.presence_visibility. It is an input to the projection rather than a property of any lease, which is why it is here and not on the lease record: the projection merges every device into one answer, so the policy that governs the answer has to be held once per account.

viewer_relationship.description: self is the participant's own surface. blocked-either-direction collapses both directions deliberately: blocks are directional as relationships, but neither party sees the other's presence, because a one-way hole is itself a signal.

availability.description: The coarse projection of the lease state, exactly the mapping the binding table in docs/architecture/AUTHORITATIVE_STATE_AND_PLATFORM_CONTRACT.md declares: absent, expired and revoked all render offline.

suppressed_reason.description: Why a viewer is shown offline for a reason other than the subject being offline. Present only when the projection was suppressed. It is never disclosed to the viewer — it exists so that a support question has an answer — because telling a viewer they were suppressed tells them the subject is online.
